title: Bea and the Starry Coral
markdown:
Bea Nkomo was an orbital park ranger. She did not patrol dusty canyons or green forests. Her park floated in the sparkly inky blackness of space. She zipped around in a trusty little ranger vessel that hummed with the quiet efficiency of a well-loved teapot. Her best friend was not a dog or a cat, but Crumb, a bot shaped like a fuzzy mischievous monkey whose favorite thing in the entire universe was stealing snacks. Little grabby paws. A sensor always on the hunt for anything remotely edible, especially if it was crunchy and zero-gravity-friendly.

Bea loved her job more than a vacuum cleaner loves dust bunnies. She zoomed through the silent star-dusted expanse of the orbital habitats, tools humming, making sure everything was just so. Her favorite place, the crown jewel of her patrol, she called the Glimmering Depths. A coral reef not of rock but of pure shimmering light and gentle currents of space-dust, dancing in weightless harmony. So delicate. So fragile. Bea was its fiercest protector.

Lately, trouble was brewing like lukewarm space-coffee. Tourists flocked to the Glimmering Depths on ships that looked like giant gleaming space-loaches. Not just to look. They insisted on touching everything. They poked and prodded the light-coral, clumsy fingers sending shivers through its glow, all for a quick selfie. Bea would sigh, a tiny puff escaping her helmet, as she cleaned up the faint trails of their passing.

“It’s like trying to herd glitter,” she’d mutter to Crumb, who was busy pilfering a shiny discarded bolt. She desperately wanted to tell her bosses this was not okay. But she had a secret wibble-wobble in her tummy whenever she thought about speaking up. Public speaking made her palms sweat, slick as an oil spill, and her voice shrink and squeak like a startled space mouse. That squirmy feeling was her own little shadow, whispering doubts.

One day a particularly enormous transport, bristling with an alarming number of selfie-sticks, was announced. Heading straight for the Depths.

“This is it,” Bea whispered. “They’ll ruin it all before I can even blink.”

Then the comms message arrived. Her promotion was being announced next week. A promotion that required a big speech in front of everyone. All the big cheeses. If she did not do something fast, the Depths would be trampled by a million tiny insistent tourist fingers. And she would have to stand on a stage and squeak. The thought made her want the nearest black hole.

With a deep breath that barely filled her lungs, and Crumb stuffed with an entire bag of space-pretzel bites snagged from a catering drone, she piloted toward the Depths. They passed swirling nebulae like cosmic tie-dye and dodged rogue space-beads tumbling like marbles. This new part of the park was even more sensitive, structures like spun sugar, shimmering with inner luminescence.

As they approached she spotted them. A gaggle of tourists already reaching out with eager grubby hands.

“No. Please don’t touch.” A tiny insignificant whisper against the vast indifferent expanse. They could not hear, or chose not to. They giggled, pointing eager fingers like tiny lasers.

Then a group of very important-looking people, bloggers with more followers than stars in a small galaxy, descended from a sleek silver shuttle, cameras already flashing. Bea’s heart did a triple backflip, landing somewhere near her left boot. She had to stop them. She tried to explain the impossibly delicate ecosystem, the microscopic organisms that formed the light-coral’s structure. Her voice would not work. A rock in her throat. A prickly blob of fear around her vocal cords. She almost turned back to hide behind a very large friendly-looking asteroid.

Suddenly Crumb, in his infinite wisdom and overwhelming hunger, spotted a stray shimmering snack wrapper floating by. It looked as if it might once have had cheese-dust. He launched from Bea’s lap, chattering, and zoomed through the tourists’ legs with the agility of greased lightning. He whooped past a blogger’s nose, snatching a tiny almost invisible crumb from a hastily consumed snack pouch. The blogger yelped, startled, then looked around in confusion. Crumb, mistaking the yelp for an invitation, started spectacular loop-de-loops, trailing the inedible wrapper like a tiny absurd kite.

Most of the tourists, amused by the zero-G monkey-bot, forgot the coral and chased the funny little bot, laughter echoing softly. So busy trying to get a video of Crumb that they left the delicate coral, for the moment, beautifully undisturbed. Bea watched, utterly amazed. Snack-mischief had accidentally saved the day for a brief precious moment.

As the last of the tourist-chasers rounded a distant asteroid, her comms crackled. “Bea. The VIPs are arriving early for your promotion announcement. Get here now.”

Her stomach plummeted like a dropped wrench. She had to leave the Depths, and she still had not found a permanent solution.

This was the apex of her personal terror. The big hall. The speech. A tremor starting in her knees. Mouth dry as a desert planet. She pictured the podium, blinding spotlights, a sea of expectant judging faces. She thought of the tourists’ careless prodding fingers and the fragile beauty they could so easily destroy. The air smelled faintly of ozone and stale coffee. Then she thought of the light-coral pulsing with ethereal light, and took a shaky step toward her ship. Soft thud of boots on deck plating. No turning back. She zoomed toward the hall, the weight of fear a tangible pressure in the small cockpit.

On the stage the bright hot lights blinded her. The low expectant murmur of the crowd made her skin prickle. She opened her mouth, and this time, instead of a squeak, a clear steady voice emerged, surprising even herself. She spoke about the Glimmering Depths, about the wonders of microgravity habitats, and then about the tourists. She explained, with surprising clarity and a touch of genuine passion, why they should not touch, why observation was its own form of appreciation. She even managed a small self-deprecating joke about Crumb’s snack-wrapper escapades. The crowd laughed. They listened. They understood. By the end her voice was strong. A standing ovation. Off the stage her legs were still a little wobbly. The promotion was hers, and with it the power to create new rules.

Later, back at the Depths, a small group of new visitors arrived armed with nothing but curiosity and a respectful distance. Bea felt a tiny flicker of the old nervousness. This time it did not freeze her. Just a whisper. She approached them with a confident smile and explained the rules, pointing out the most beautiful sections without ever getting too close. Crumb munched a specially made giant space-cookie, tail wagging. The light-coral pulsed gently, safe. Bea did not announce that her voice was as bright as the stars. She only posted the new guideline on the park channel, one line, no touching, and let Crumb lick sugar from a grabby paw while the coral kept its own light.
characters: Bea Nkomo (orbital park ranger), Crumb (snack-stealing monkey-bot)
